note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 2 months of low energy, insomnia, low mood, decreased appetite and libido, poor concentration, and new exertional shortness of breath; past hypothyroidism on levothyroxine; plan for in-person exam and blood tests. DDx includes depressive/adjustment disorder, thyroid dysfunction, and anemia (consistent with transcript and DDx).

History:
- Presenting complaint: Low energy and difficulty getting up in the morning; daily activities feel harder than usual.
- Timeline: Symptoms began around the time he started a new job (~2 months ago). Initially described as “last few weeks,” clarified to ~2 months; persistent.
- Sleep: Trouble sleeping; not waking early but difficulty sleeping at all.
- Appetite: Reduced.
- Mood/cognition: Lower mood recently; easily distracted; difficulty focusing; sometimes still enjoys activities.
- Libido/sexual function: Decreased sex drive over the past few months. Change in morning erections: conflicting responses (initially “not noticed recently,” later “no change” — conflict noted).
- Dyspnea: Shortness of breath with sports/exertion over the past few months, worse than baseline.
- Safety: Denies suicidal or homicidal thoughts.
- Pertinent negatives: No visual changes reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (on treatment).
- No prior mental health diagnoses reported.
- No other chronic conditions documented.

Medications:
- Levothyroxine (Thyroxine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known medication allergies reported. Other allergies not documented.

Social History:
- Married.
- Started a new job ~2 months ago (temporal association with symptom onset).
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not recorded.
- Occupation details: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Father died by suicide ~15 years ago.
- Otherwise noncontributory per patient (mother well; only child; no known family depression reported).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded (video consult only).

Investigations:
- None obtained during this encounter.
- Plan stated to arrange in-person examination and blood tests (specific tests not listed in transcript).

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Subacute (≈2 months) fatigue, insomnia, low mood, reduced appetite and libido, impaired concentration, and exertional dyspnea temporally associated with a job change. History of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Denies suicidality. Working impression: depressive/adjustment disorder vs thyroid dysfunction; consider anemia; insomnia likely contributory.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Major depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood: Supported by low mood, insomnia, low energy, reduced appetite, poor concentration, decreased interest/libido, onset after job change; partially opposed by some preserved enjoyment and no SI.
  - Thyroid dysfunction (under- or over-replacement): Supported by known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine with fatigue/low mood/low libido; insomnia and exertional dyspnea could reflect over-replacement; lacks classic directional features.
  - Anemia (e.g., iron deficiency): Supported by fatigue and new exertional dyspnea; no corroborating signs reported.
  - Hypogonadism: Possible given decreased libido; morning erections history conflicting — conflict noted.

- Issue 1: Low mood, fatigue, poor concentration, insomnia (possible depressive/adjustment disorder; insomnia contributory)
  - Plan:
    - In-person assessment with mental health screening (e.g., PHQ-9/GAD-7) and sleep assessment.
    - Provide sleep hygiene guidance and stress management supports.
    - Discuss psychosocial supports/brief counseling; consider therapy referral depending on in-person assessment.
    - Safety net: If suicidal thoughts emerge, seek urgent care/emergency services immediately.
    - Follow up after labs and exam.

- Issue 2: Known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine; possible dosing/thyroid dysfunction
  - Plan:
    - Check thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) and review levothyroxine adherence and timing.
    - Continue levothyroxine as currently prescribed until reviewed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Adjust therapy based on results in primary care.

- Issue 3: Exertional shortness of breath and fatigue (consider anemia; cardiorespiratory causes less likely but not excluded)
  - Plan:
    - Order CBC with indices; consider iron studies (ferritin, iron, TIBC) based on results.
    - Physical exam with vitals and cardiorespiratory exam at in-person visit.
    - Safety net: Seek urgent care if chest pain, resting/worsening shortness of breath, syncope, or new concerning symptoms occur.

- General plan items:
  - Blood tests as part of initial workup (per transcript). Reasonable options to consider, guided by DDx: CMP, vitamin B12/folate, vitamin D; consider morning total testosterone if low libido persists after addressing mood/thyroid.
  - Nutrition and activity as tolerated.
  - Arrange GP appointment in the next few days for exam and labs; follow-up to review results and refine plan.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, physical exam, comprehensive ROS, medication dose/route/frequency, non-medication allergies, tobacco/alcohol/substance use, occupational details.
- Conflicts: Morning erections history (initially “not noticed recently,” later “no change”) — conflict noted. Initial duration “few weeks” later clarified to ~2 months (clarified, not conflicting).
- Transcript quality: Minor communication issues/connection freeze; otherwise intelligible.
